known_stress_episodes.note: New home sales peaked mid-2005 and collapsed ~80% into 2009 — a classic leading signal ahead of the GFC.

known_stress_episodes.note: Sales surged on low rates then reversed as rates rose.

known_stress_episodes.note: Mortgage-rate shock crushed new home sales; strong recent regime captured in the OOS window.

key_finding: Lead-lag: New Home Sales YoY Granger-causes SPY at lags [11]; reverse SPY->NHS significant at lags [1, 2]. The IS-selected tournament winner (NHS contraction, T2_roll_p25, P2_signal_strength counter, lead 9m) is countercyclical: IS Sharpe 1.46 vs buy-and-hold 0.79; OOS Sharpe 0.93 vs 0.89, OOS HAC t 3.26, max drawdown -13.5% vs -23.9%.
mechanism: New Home Sales is an early-cycle housing-demand indicator: buyers commit before construction, so sales lead starts, permits, and the employment/consumption they drive. Stronger home-sales growth coincides with a healthier cycle and better equities (procyclical). The tradable edge is a 2-state HMM regime probability on deseasonalised YoY growth, timing SPY exposure to the favourable housing regime.
caveats: Forward Granger causality is weak (NHS->SPY significant only at lag 11; reverse SPY->NHS at lags 1-2).
Winner is the max of 5,297 valid combinations; bootstrap p=0.071 (NOT significant at 5%).
In-sample Sharpe 0.81 vs OOS 1.49; found_in_search, no holdout final exam yet.
OOS window (2018+) is short and episode-concentrated; durability only conditionally_durable.
Indicator is NSA; all signals are YoY/STL-deseasonalised, raw level excluded.
narrative_summary: Procyclical, leading housing-demand signal. HMM regime Long/Cash overlay: OOS Sharpe 1.49 vs 0.89 B&H, max DD -8.3% vs -23.9%. Low confidence: weak forward causality, non-significant bootstrap, short episode-concentrated OOS.
